tldr: Indian startups raised only about $113–123 Mn this week across 28 deals, down roughly 72% from the week before.
Personal care brand Nat Habit raised ₹142 Cr, led by Trident Growth Partners, to go from about 20,000 to 2 lakh shops.
Peak XV sold about ₹30 Cr of co-working company Awfis's shares, continuing to cut its stake.
Cleantech startups raised $433 Mn in Q3 2026, almost four times a year earlier, led by electric-vehicle makers.

stories.title: Startup funding falls about 72% in a quiet week
stories.summary: Indian startups raised about $113 Mn across 28 deals in the week of 5 to 10 October, according to Entrackr, down about 72% from $411 Mn the week before. Inc42 counted about $123 Mn. Most deals were small: 22 were early-stage. The biggest were DailyObjects (₹332 Cr), Beyond Appliances (₹110 Cr) and NeoGrowth (₹85 Cr).
stories.whyItMatters: Weekly totals swing a lot because one big deal can double them. Many small early-stage deals and few large ones suggest investors are still cautious with big cheques.

stories.title: Nat Habit raises ₹142 Cr to get into 2 lakh shops
stories.summary: Nat Habit, a D2C personal care brand selling ayurvedic-style hair oils, masks and face creams, raised ₹142 Cr in a Series C led by Trident Growth Partners, with existing and new investors. It says its annual gross revenue run-rate is ₹330 Cr. It wants to grow from about 20,000 offline stores to 2 lakh in three years and launch sunscreens and serums.
stories.whyItMatters: Many online-first brands are now moving into physical shops, because that is where most Indian shoppers still buy. Offline expansion is expensive, which is why brands raise large rounds for it.

stories.title: Peak XV sells ₹30 Cr of Awfis shares
stories.summary: An affiliate of Peak XV Partners sold 12.2 lakh shares of Awfis, a listed co-working company, for about ₹29.8 Cr at ₹245 each in a bulk deal. Peak XV has now sold more than half of its holding.
stories.whyItMatters: This is a VC exit in action: after a company lists on the stock market, its early investors sell shares in steps to return money to their own investors.

stories.title: OTPless hires ex-BharatPe executive Geetanshu Singla as CTO
stories.summary: Login and authentication startup OTPless appointed Geetanshu Singla, formerly at BharatPe, as its chief technology officer.
stories.whyItMatters: Senior hires are a signal of where a startup is heading. Investors watch whether a company can attract experienced leaders as it grows.

stories.title: Cleantech funding jumps to $433 Mn in Q3, led by EV makers
stories.summary: Indian cleantech startups raised $433 Mn across 23 deals in July to September 2026, up from $118 Mn across 16 deals a year earlier. Electric-vehicle companies made up 57% of deals. River ($120 Mn), Yulu ($93 Mn) and Ultraviolette ($85 Mn) together took nearly 69% of the money.
stories.whyItMatters: When a few big rounds make up most of a sector's funding, investors are concentrating on likely winners rather than spreading bets widely.

stories.title: Markets end an eight-week losing streak; MobiKwik jumps 25%
stories.summary: The Sensex rose 0.78% and the Nifty 0.44% this week, ending an eight-week losing run, even after the Nifty touched a 52-week low midweek. Among listed new-age tech companies, 36 of 66 gained. MobiKwik rose nearly 25%, partly on hopes of UPI merchant fees, and PhysicsWallah rose about 20%.
stories.whyItMatters: Listed startup share prices set the mood for private funding. When public investors pay more for tech companies, VCs can more easily raise money and value private startups higher.

concept.explanation: A bulk deal is a share trade on the stock exchange in which one buyer or seller trades more than 0.5% of a listed company's shares in a single day. Exchanges publish the names of the parties, so everyone can see who bought or sold. It is different from a block deal, which is one large trade (usually ₹10 Cr or more) done in a special trading window.
concept.example: Peak XV sold 12.2 lakh Awfis shares in a bulk deal this week. Because bulk deals are made public, we know the buyer of most of those shares was Kritagyata Trust.
